close_reason: Added SetError::validate_extras returning Result<(), ReservedExtrasKey>. Deterministic across build profiles unlike the existing with_extra debug_assert. ReservedExtrasKey is pub, #[non_exhaustive], Display+Error. Field doc gained a 'Reserved-name invariant' block pointing at the method. Two tests: positive control + iterates every reserved wire-name. The pub(crate) option from the bead was rejected because it would violate workspace AGENTS.md 'extras-preservation policy: pub extra'. The Serialize-panic option was rejected because it requires manual Serialize impl. Landed at additive surface-narrowing — direct mutation still compiles, but consumers and tests have a deterministic gate.
description:
crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:69 — SetError.extra is declared as `pub
extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>` directly on the struct.
The struct is #[non_exhaustive] (blocks struct literal from outside) and
ships a `with_extra(key, value)` builder whose debug_assert rejects keys
that collide with reserved typed-field wire-names
(RESERVED_SET_ERROR_WIRE_NAMES). Direct field mutation bypasses that guard:

    let mut e = SetError::new(SetErrorType::custom("rateLimited"));
    e.extra.insert("type".to_string(), json!("evil"));   // compiles, no warning

The resulting wire shape carries two `type` keys at the same level. RFC
8259 §4 calls duplicate-key behaviour implementation-defined; in practice
many JMAP clients silently take the last value and the SetError is
malformed.

What callers cannot depend on: that emitting a SetError via the
documented `new() + with_*` builder chain is sufficient to avoid the
malformed-wire-shape footgun. The reserved-name guard is a debug_assert
only because the builder API is the assumed access path; the public
field surface invalidates that assumption.

What goes wrong when this stays as-is: a future contributor (handler
author, test helper, mock-backend builder) reaches for `e.extra.insert`
directly because the field is `pub`, ships the call, and the bug is
only caught by manual wire-shape inspection — there is no test gate
because debug_assert is bypassed.

Resolution paths (one is sufficient):
- Make `extra` `pub(crate)` and expose read access via an accessor.
  Mutation forced through `with_extra`.
- Keep `extra` pub but add a runtime assertion in `serde::Serialize`
  that panics on reserved-name collision, so the bug surfaces at the
  first serialize call (matches the existing debug_assert philosophy).
- Document the contract: "Direct mutation of `extra` is supported but
  callers MUST avoid keys in RESERVED_SET_ERROR_WIRE_NAMES; the
  `with_extra` helper enforces this in debug builds."

The same concern applies to every typed result struct in backend.rs
with `pub` fields exposed via builders (ChangesResult, QueryResult,
QueryChangesResult, AddedItem), but those have no analogue validation
guard for `with_extra` to bypass, so the issue is unique to SetError.
title: SetError.extra is pub — bypasses with_extra reserved-name validation
